name: Conversion engine
outcome: Docker strategy becomes the buildah ClusterBuildStrategy, S2I becomes source-to-image | Git, binary, image and inline-Dockerfile sources all convert | The plugin whiteouts the BuildConfig and emits the Build over the crane plugin protocol | Runs offline, never talks to a cluster

name: Image references and registries
outcome: ImageStream references resolve through --imagestream-mapping and --registry-mapping | No match falls back to the internal registry URL, with a warning | Search, insecure and block registry lists pass through as strategy params | You can redirect output off the internal registry, and the plugin warns when that breaks an ImageStream watcher

name: Buildah option parity
outcome: noCache, forcePull and squash become the no-cache, pull and squash params | dockerStrategy.from becomes runtime-stage-from | buildArgs carry over, including ConfigMap and Secret references | The shipped buildah strategy declares every one of these params

name: S2I option parity
outcome: The builder image becomes the builder-image param | Custom scripts, incremental builds and forcePull have params in the shipped strategy | The plugin still drops those three with an RFE warning
status_note: the strategy already has the params

name: Credentials, ServiceAccounts and volumes
outcome: A pull secret lands on a generated ServiceAccount | The plugin never overwrites a named ServiceAccount, it prints the oc command to link the secret instead | A missing push credential gets a warning that names it | Secret and ConfigMap volumes carry over with the exact strategy edit they need | Source secrets and ConfigMaps get a runbook instead of a half migration

name: BuildConfig field coverage
outcome: Labels and annotations copy over, minus the OpenShift-managed ones | completionDeadlineSeconds becomes spec.timeout | nodeSelector and the two history limits map to their Shipwright fields | Image labels become output labels | Resources become a BuildRun template in an annotation

name: Conversion outcome and warnings
outcome: Each BuildConfig ends as converted, converted with warnings, skipped or failed, recorded on the object | A lossy conversion can never look clean | One bad BuildConfig never aborts the run | 62 warnings, each catalogued with what to do about it

name: Triggers, preserved not converted
outcome: On OpenShift a BuildConfig starts builds by itself, from a git webhook, a new base image or a change to its own config. After migration nothing does: Builds for Red Hat OpenShift 1.9 ships no component that reads Shipwright's trigger section | The plugin keeps every trigger as sanitised JSON in an annotation on the Build, secrets and image IDs stripped, so they can be rebuilt once a triggers component exists | It warns once per trigger with the replacement: repoint the git webhook to Pipelines-as-Code or Tekton Triggers, start image-change builds from your own automation, create the first BuildRun by hand | The runbook that walks through those steps per trigger type is BUILD-2393, not started
status_note: nothing fires by itself on the target. BUILD-1706 and BUILD-2074 would change that, both New

name: Safe migration runs
outcome: Converting twice gives byte-identical output | Generated names are valid DNS labels with a hash suffix and collision handling | No dry-run flag, because transform never touches a cluster

name: Test infrastructure and CI
outcome: Unit tests with a coverage gate in CI | A transform E2E script | A Minikube cluster E2E run on every PR | A YAML-rules E2E framework with 18 real BuildConfigs, in review

name: Documentation and examples
outcome: Architecture page, support matrix, three worked examples, README rewrite and eight decision records are on main since 2026-09-03 | The volume runbook is on main | Trigger runbook, crane help text and the blog are not started

name: Agent skills and workflow
outcome: Seven Claude Code skills under .claude/skills in the plugin repo: tech-design with setup-repos, tech-implement, tech-review, tech-test, tech-document, deep-review and create-pr | Together they carry a story from design through implementation, review, test, docs and PR | Two audit process chores were closed without work

name: Param names match the shipped strategies
outcome: Every setting the plugin writes into a Build must exist under the same name in the buildah or source-to-image strategy on the target, or Shipwright refuses to register the Build | They match today. The five params added in 2026 landed in strategy-catalog and the operator ships a copy | Unit tests pin all ten names, and the Minikube E2E registers Builds against upstream sample strategies, which cover the base names only | A check inside the plugin was built in PR #58 and dropped: a wrong name already fails loudly, and a bundled copy cannot tell which operator release the target runs
status_note: names match today, catalog-only params verified by hand

name: Upstream API and dependency alignment
outcome: The Shipwright omitempty API change shipped upstream | The plugin pins Shipwright v0.20.11 and a crane-lib pseudo-version | crane consuming omitempty waits on Shipwright v0.21

name: Destination pre-flight checks
outcome: Would verify Shipwright, Tekton, the strategies and RBAC on the target before apply | Filed in May 2026 against the live crane convert, which could reach a cluster | The offline design came later. PR #1 on 2026-08-11 made the converter a crane plugin that never calls a cluster, and ADR-0001 records that rule | Closed Won't Do on 2026-08-17 because the check can no longer run where the code lives
